correctness.rationale: The exact finite-window Mecke covariance is a convolution of the start-event conditional-coverage kernel with triangular window weight. The kernel is absolutely integrable under E[L²]<∞, allowing dominated convergence. Integrating the stop-loss derivative gives the covariance-density identity. Jensen implies h(t)≥(μ−t)+, making every Taylor coefficient after the linear term negative; this establishes exactly one positive zero, sharp deterministic bound, and second-moment bound. Stop-loss characterization establishes convex-order monotonicity and strictness. The numerical verifier independently checks 322 finite-atomic and deterministic identities. No extrapolation from finite tests is used.

originality.rationale: The general existence and formulas for asymptotic intrinsic-volume covariances of Boolean models are established in Hug–Last–Schulte, arXiv:1308.6519 (Corollary 6.2 and Theorems 3.1, 6.1), so the density formula alone is not asserted to be new. The inspected sections do not contain the one-dimensional universal unique-zero theorem for every finite-second-moment grain distribution, the entire-curve convex-order ordering, or its sharp deterministic crossover bound. These require a global coefficient-sign and stop-loss comparison beyond merely specifying a covariance. The CWI 1995 germ–grain CLT and 1992 Poisson clump article are further historical risks; exhaustive priority is not certified.
residual_risks: The strongest prior general mixed covariance theorem could make the density identity implicit; only the new single-zero, sharp extremal and convex-order conclusions are evaluated as novel.
The 1992 cluster-analysis full text remained inaccessible; it might contain a relevant special case.
Older one-dimensional renewal/clump literature not exhaustively surveyed; originality is a self-review, not independent priority certification.

value.rationale: The competition between increasing component starts and merging occupied intervals is a natural coverage statistic. The claimed theorem classifies the covariance sign for all intensities and all positive finite-second-moment grain laws, provides a sharp fixed-mean extremal threshold, and orders the entire covariance curves under increased grain heterogeneity. Neither mere correctness nor a recomputed known covariance formula is presented as the value; the structural one-crossing and variability principle supplies that value.
